Iranian Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Esmail Baqaei has rejected baseless claims by Kaja Kallas, the European Union’s foreign policy chief, alleging Iran’s interference in the Saudi Arabia-Yemen conflict, stating that the European Union itself is complicit in gross human rights violations in Yemen due to its participation in sanctions and the economic blockade imposed on the Yemeni people. He stressed that European officials cannot absolve themselves of responsibility through blame-shifting remarks. The Foreign Ministry spokesperson also categorically rejected claims about the presence of Iranian military experts in Yemen, stressing that the dissemination of such fake reports is intended to cover up the realities and divert public attention. Baqaei noted that the Yemeni people have demonstrated that they possess the necessary capabilities, experience, courage, and determination to defend their national sovereignty and human dignity, and have no need for the intervention of any party in this regard. Condemning military attacks on various parts of Yemen, particularly civilian facilities, vital infrastructure, and residential areas, which have resulted in the martyrdom of more than 270 Yemeni Muslims, including 130 children and women, and injured over 650 others, as well as the destruction of infrastructure and people's homes, Baqaei called for an end to acts of aggression against Yemen's national sovereignty and territorial integrity. Reiterating Iran's principled position on the ongoing conflict in the Arabian Peninsula, the Foreign Ministry spokesperson stressed that establishing peace in the Arabian Peninsula requires an end to military attacks, respect for the Yemeni people's right to self-determination, the lifting of the naval and aerial blockade imposed on the country, and dialogue based on the roadmap agreed upon by Yemenis and Saudi Arabia. He added that the Islamic Republic of Iran is ready to provide any assistance in this regard. Criticizing the continued exploitation of the UN Security Council to justify the inhumane blockade of Yemen, Baqaei stressed the need for an immediate halt to military attacks and the complete lifting of the blockade and illegal restrictions imposed on the country.

item.title: Iranian ambassador to Poland meets FM Araghchi
item.description: Isa Kameli, Ambassador of the Islamic Republic of Iran to Poland, met and held talks with Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi on Wednesday afternoon. During the meeting, Kameli presented a report on Iran-Poland bilateral relations and developments concerning the European Union. The Foreign Minister, recalling the Islamic Republic of Iran’s policy of strengthening diplomatic approaches, the rule of law, and multilateralism at the international level, stressed the importance of making use of all opportunities to articulate Iran’s positions and expand relations with other countries.

item.title: Araghchi: Iran seeks regional security arrangements without foreign military presence
item.description:
Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi said in a post on X that he had stressed during an interview with Al Jazeera that Iran harbors no hostility toward Persian Gulf Cooperation Council member states, appreciates Qatar and Oman’s positive role, and continues its dialogue with Saudi Arabia. He added that Iran seeks new regional security arrangements shaped by the countries of the region themselves, without the presence of foreign military forces.

The two countries share numerous historical, cultural, familial, political and economic ties, and both have always demonstrated the political will to preserve and strengthen their relations. Today's visit was also very productive. Detailed explanations were provided to the president and foreign minister of Turkmenistan regarding the latest regional developments, the negotiations, and the readiness of our armed forces. Subsequently, key economic projects between the two countries were reviewed, and important decisions were made regarding their implementation.

FM Araghchi: Iran ready for honest diplomacy, will not bow to pressure Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi made the following remarks regarding indirect negotiations between Iran and the United States: Given the sensitivity of the current situation, consultations and diplomatic engagements have become very intensive. Qatar and Pakistan, as mediators, are playing a very active role. We have stated our conditions and presented our proposal, and everything depends on Washington's political rationality. If they choose honest diplomacy, we are ready to engage. But if they intend to resort to deception and military operations, they will face a response more bitter and severe than in the past. Tehran's conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz are completely clear and transparent. If these conditions are accepted, the Strait of Hormuz will be reopened and negotiations will resume. Otherwise, the current situation will continue, and Iran will not bow. The consultations held by the Deputy Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council in Beijing were conducted within the framework of ongoing strategic communications with key partners. Broad regional developments, security issues, and matters related to peace and war were discussed.

item.title: Iranian FM meets with Turkmen President Foreign Minister
item.description: At the start of his visit to Turkmenistan, Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi met with President Serdar Berdimuhamedov and discussed the most important bilateral political and economic issues between the two countries. During the meeting, the two sides, referring to the history of friendly relations and the cultural and civilizational ties between the two countries, stressed the need to expand these relations. Later in his visit to Ashgabat, Araghchi met and held talks with Turkmen Foreign Minister Rashid Meredov. During the meeting, the Iranian foreign minister, emphasizing the neighborhood policy in the foreign relations strategy of the 14th administration of the Islamic Republic of Iran, described the expansion of relations between the two countries in the political, economic and parliamentary fields as important. The Turkmen foreign minister, for his part, highlighting the significance of the visit by the Iranian diplomatic delegation, reaffirmed his country's readiness to develop political and economic relations with Iran within both bilateral and international frameworks. The Iranian foreign minister and his accompanying delegation departed Ashgabat for Tehran on Monday evening.

item.title: Iranian FM congratulates Algeria on National Day
item.description: Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi, in a message to Algerian Foreign Minister Ahmed Attaf, congratulated the Algerian nation and government on the 72nd anniversary of the launch of the liberation revolution and Algeria’s National Day. In his message, the Iranian foreign minister wished prosperity and well-being for the government and great people of Algeria and expressed hope that Iran and Algeria, by continuing their active and constructive approach in supporting justice-oriented causes, would see their joint efforts strengthened and make greater use of their existing capacities to further expand cooperation at the bilateral, regional, and international levels.

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic of Iran, while condemning the anti-Iranian policies and actions of the British government, which are contrary to the principles of the United Nations Charter and international law, particularly the principle of respect for national sovereignty and the prohibition of resorting to unlawful measures against other countries, reaffirms the determination of the Government of the Islamic Republic of Iran to take the necessary measures to safeguard Iran’s national security and interests. Accordingly, and pursuant to a resolution of the country’s Supreme National Security Council, in response to the British government’s hostile actions against the Islamic Republic of Iran over the past year, including its involvement in the US-Israeli imposed war against Iran through the provision of military and logistical bases and facilities located in territories under British jurisdiction, as well as that government’s decision on July 13, 2026 to place the Islamic Revolution Guard Corps (IRGC) under the State Threats Act 2026, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs announces the following: A) As of the issuance of this statement (November 1, 2026), the UK’s Secret Intelligence Service (MI6) shall be classified as a “hostile group” pursuant to Note 2 to Article 1 of the Law on “Enhancing Punishments for Espionage and Cooperation with the Zionist Regime and Hostile Countries Against National Security and Interests,” and the provisions of this law shall apply to the British agency B) As of the issuance of this statement (November 1, 2026), the UK’s Royal Navy and Royal Air Force shall be subject to the Law on “Countermeasures Against the United States’ Designation of the Islamic Revolution Guard Corps as a Terrorist Organization” and shall accordingly be designated as terrorist organizations. It is self-evident that these measures have been adopted in accordance with the principles of international law and within the framework of the principle of reciprocity, and the British government shall bear responsibility for their consequences.

Iranian Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Esmaeil Baqaei condemned the Canadian prime minister for echoing the UAE’s baseless claim to Iran’s three islands in the Persian Gulf, describing the move as a blatant contradiction and a flagrant violation of the principles of the UN Charter in a post on X. "The UAE was established in 1971. Yet, despite the overwhelming historical record ، geographical facts and documented evidence concerning Abu Musa and the Greater Tunb and Lesser Tunb, it lays claim to these IRANIAN islands whose history of being part of IRAN stretches back many millennia before the establishment of the federation itself. Remarkably, Canada's Prime Minister has chosen to echo this absurd claim! Canada, of all countries, must understand the importance of territorial integrity and national sovereignty as its own history is marked by the American invasion during the War of 1812, the Montreal Annexation Manifesto of 1849, and, more recently, Donald Trump's repeated threats to turn Canada into the 51st state of the United States. A country that has spent more than two centuries defending its territorial integrity against the ambitions of its southern neighbour - how can it take sides in a fabricated dispute and endorse an unfounded territorial claim that amounts to dangerous adventurism? Is territorial integrity and respect for historical and legal facts a fundamental principle for Canada, or does it matter only when Canada's own sovereignty is at stake? Does Canada not realize that, in doing so, it is effectively sawing off the very branch on which it sits?"
